screens.explain: Estimates cut into the print (revision tercile T1): beats have paid more here.

screens.label: High bar

blocks.text: Value now (forward PE against the industry and the name's own history, the peer premium vs the premium its growth and quality earn, gap = cheaper than its profile when positive) and forward (street upside, the forward-value base price and IRR vs its hurdle, the growth the price assumes, revisions). source.sql: SELECT c.symbol, c.react_on, c.slot, c.mcap_b, c.ind, b.close, b.pe_nfy, b.pe_nfy_vs_ind, b.pe_nfy_vs_own, b.peer_mult, b.peer_prem_pct, b.peer_just_pct, b.peer_gap_pct, b.peer_px_fit, b.evebitda, b.peg_fwd, b.fcf_margin, b.nd_ebitda, b.pt_up, b.street_px, b.fv_base_px, b.fv_upside_pct, b.irr_exp_pct, b.hurdle_pct, b.priced_in_cagr_pct, b.fwd_eps_g, b.rev_yoy, b.eps_rev_3m, b.rev_rev_3m, b.pt_drift_3m, b.analysts FROM cards c LEFT JOIN read_csv_auto('{PACK}/board/names.csv') b USING (symbol) ORDER BY c.react_on, c.book_usd DESC NULLS LAST, c.mcap_b DESC

screens.label: Cheaper than its profile
screens.explain: Gap over +15%: cheaper than peers with the same growth and quality.

screens.label: Rich to its profile
screens.explain: Gap under -25%: the print has to carry a premium its profile does not earn.

screens.label: IRR over hurdle
screens.explain: Forward-value base price over the close.

screens.label: Estimates rising
screens.explain: 3-month EPS revision up: read the bar (raised estimates = high bar).

blocks.text: Strength (trailing returns, the alpha model's 28-day decile and forecast, up/down volume, trend quality, lenses) and technical position (rsi, range, 50-day and 200-day, ATR, the bounce band and kill, event warning).

guide.intro: A card is a short read of one reporter built only from the pack's numbers; nothing on it is a score. Course, Grade, the Judgment line and Notes (OUTSIDE) are the judgment's.

sections.title: Reading a card
rows: Header
Id, company, industry, slot (BMO before the open / AMC after the close), print date, market cap in $B, and the judgment's Course / Grade / Horizon.
Headline
The set-up into the print, forward PE against the industry and its own median, the pointer counts and the name's average print move.
Metrics
Hover for the Ledger meaning. Counts h28 / h7 are measured pointers up / down; tail_starter_usd is a $5,000 starter's overnight bad case.
Going into the print
The tape into the print, the previous print, the set-up cell's measured hold and overnight tail, the deterioration state.
Value, cash flow and the street
Cheap or rich against the industry and its own history, cash generation, leverage, the street target and how it moved.
What the quarter has to show
The bar: consensus against last quarter's reported numbers; whether estimates were raised into the print (top quintile = priced) or cut (a lower bar).
Industry and peers
Where the name sits among its peers, and how the industry's prints were paid in the last 35 days: a punished industry raises the bar.
Pointers and the model
Which measured pointers point up / down per horizon, the alpha deciles with their measured record, the model's drivers.
Levels and size
Where to buy after the print (buy-in-red band), where the thesis dies (kill), the dollars a starter risks overnight.
What to read on the print
A checklist: the bar, the mix cells, the after-hours rule, the set-up's kill rule, the size, the down pointers.

sections.title: Before the print, in four steps
items: Focus tab: the Book's prints first. Hold vs DERISK comes from the down pointers, the overnight tail against what you accept, and the bar.
Leans up: open the card, check the families (Tape pointers move together), the bar (estimates priced?) and the industry's season. A pre-print entry is a hold-through bet, not a reaction call.
No down pointer in Estimates or History and a tail you accept: an event ticket from the Daily's budget, limit in the band. Otherwise wait for the print and use the bounce band.
Leans down: no pre-print long; note the bounce band for after the print.

sections.title: After the print
items: Re-run print-night and print-brief after the post-close scan (or with --react-on today the next morning): the Printed tab fills.
Read rev_posted, then the mix and the After the print section; decide at the cash close.

sections.title: What the cards do not have yet
items: Management guidance, the earnings release text, call commentary and news: these come only as the judgment's Notes (OUTSIDE), written per name. A filings module (SEC 8-K Item 2.02 press releases) is the planned follow-up.

rows: E
On: next-FY EPS estimate cut by more than 1% over about 3 months (panel eps_rev_3m < -1). Off: held or raised. Unknown (?): no positive estimate 3 months ago or now.
R
On: next-FY revenue estimate cut by more than 1% over about 3 months (rev_rev_3m < -1). Off: held or raised. Unknown (?): no estimate.
C
On: free cash flow margin (ttm) under 0, the business burns cash. Off: FCF positive. Unknown (?): no FCF margin (banks, some ADRs).
S
On: last reported EPS under its estimate (last_surprise < 0). Off: met or beat. Unknown (?): no surprise on file.
In det_seen only: that letter's field is empty, so the letter count and the count cells are empty for the name.
What the print needs
Judgment column: the beat-bar cell's surprise threshold (c_bar_text), what a beat paid on the night (c_rx_beat) and the share of beats sold (c_beat_sold) for that cell.
Value now / forward
Judgment column: forward PE and its percent to the industry median, the peer gap (positive = cheaper than its profile earns), the forward-value base price vs the close and the expected IRR.
Strength / tech
Judgment column: the alpha model's 28-day decile, the run into the print, the 50-day position, rsi, and the industry's season reaction.
